name: Laptop-Price-Prediction
description: Full-stack ML app predicting laptop prices from specs. Random Forest model (R²=0.886) served via FastAPI, React + Vite frontend with dynamic dropdowns sourced from the trained data. Live demo included.

paragraphs: A full-stack machine learning application that predicts a laptop's price from its hardware and software specifications — a trained Random Forest Regression model served through a FastAPI backend, with a React + Vite frontend for the UI.

The frontend never hardcodes dropdown values. Instead, it pulls valid options live from the backend's /options endpoint, which reflects exactly what the trained model actually saw during training — so users can never submit a combination the model wasn't trained on.
The user fills in specs — company, type, RAM, weight, display, CPU, storage, GPU, OS — on the React frontend. That request hits the FastAPI backend, which:
features: Re-derives the same engineered features used at training time (pixel density, CPU category, OS category)
Runs the feature vector through the saved Scikit-learn pipeline
Reverses the log-transform applied to the target and returns the predicted price
